subsystems.name: Segmented primary mirror
subsystems.role: a roughly 6 m aperture that folds for launch and unfolds in space, gathering enough light to see a planet a billion times fainter than its star.

subsystems.name: Coronagraph
subsystems.role: blocks the star's glare so the planet beside it becomes visible — suppression of about ten billion to one.

subsystems.name: Wavefront sensing and control
subsystems.role: measures and corrects the tiniest optical errors, keeping the starlight cancelled.

subsystems.name: Spacecraft and thermal structure
subsystems.role: holds the telescope so still and so cold that nothing drifts during a long exposure.

subsystems.name: Science instruments
subsystems.role: turn the faint planet light into a spectrum that can be searched for gases.

subsystems.name: Ground system
subsystems.role: runs long, faint-signal observations and subtracts residual starlight afterwards.

buildSteps.title: Mature the critical technologies
buildSteps.detail: Deformable mirrors, photon-counting detectors, segment stability and coronagraph masks are tested on optical benches inside vacuum chambers, with a simulated star and planet, until they reach the contrast the mission needs.

buildSteps.title: Settle the architecture
buildSteps.detail: Engineers fix the aperture size, coronagraph type and orbit — most likely Sun–Earth L2, where the Sun, Earth and Moon stay roughly behind the sunshade.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the mirror segments
buildSteps.detail: Lightweight glass or beryllium blanks are ground, polished to nanometre smoothness and coated, then measured interferometrically to verify their shape.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the optical bench
buildSteps.detail: The telescope structure, coronagraph and instruments are built on a single stable bench, then tested end-to-end in a thermal-vacuum chamber to prove the contrast survives real conditions.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the spacecraft
buildSteps.detail: Sunshade, solar arrays, propulsion, communications and thermal control are attached around the telescope.

buildSteps.title: Test the whole observatory
buildSteps.detail: Vibration, acoustic and thermal-vacuum tests simulate launch and space; the coronagraph is re-verified after each.

buildSteps.title: Launch to L2
buildSteps.detail: A heavy-lift rocket carries the folded observatory away from Earth; over weeks the sunshade opens and the mirror segments unfold.

buildSteps.title: Commission the optics
buildSteps.detail: Months of work align the segments and tune the deformable mirrors until starlight is cancelled by roughly ten billion to one.

buildSteps.title: Observe and analyse
buildSteps.detail: Each target may need tens to hundreds of hours; the planet's spectrum is extracted and searched for water, oxygen, ozone and methane.

prerequisites.why: the James Webb Space Telescope proved that a folded segmented mirror can unfold and align itself in space.
coronagraphs work on ground telescopes and a technology-demonstration instrument is planned for a space telescope, but nothing has yet reached the contrast needed for an Earth-sized planet.
the starlight cancellation only holds if the optics stay still to a fraction of an atom's width for hours.

prerequisites.tech: Photon-counting detectors for visible and ultraviolet light
prerequisites.why: detectors must register single photons from a very faint source with almost no added noise.
the folded observatory is large and heavy, so it needs a big rocket and a big fairing.

pathway.milestone: early design and technology maturation, following the 2020 astronomy decadal survey that recommended such a telescope
pathway.unlocks: a funded concept, a project office and a list of technologies that must be proven first.
evidence that starlight suppression survives launch and the space environment.

pathway.milestone: formal mission start — preliminary design, then detailed design and construction
pathway.unlocks: hardware fabrication and a firm launch date, currently foreseen in the 2040s.

pathway.milestone: launch to L2, commissioning and first reflected-light spectra of small planets
pathway.unlocks: the first real chance to look for signs of life in the air of an Earth-sized world.

pathway.milestone: larger apertures or a separate flying starshade
pathway.unlocks: shorter observations, more planets surveyed and spectra of fainter, more distant worlds.
